candidate.blueprint_locator: Printed p.7, Management of Care — Collaborate with interdisciplinary team members when providing client care; Manage care to meet client needs
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize interprofessional education as preparation for effective communication, role understanding, and collaboration across health professions in team-based care.

options.A: Limit collaboration to administrative tasks so clinical decisions remain isolated within each profession.
options.B: Replace profession-specific education so all health professions develop an identical scope of practice.
options.C: Keep professions separated during training to avoid overlap in communication, roles, or team responsibilities.
options.D: Prepare learners to communicate, understand professional roles, and collaborate effectively in interprofessional team-based care.

candidate.rationale: IPEC's current Core Competencies for Interprofessional Collaborative Practice, Version 3, are intended to prepare learners for interprofessional collaboration and teamwork to improve person/client care and population health outcomes. The framework addresses values and ethics, roles and responsibilities, communication, and teams/teamwork. D reflects that purpose. A and C contradict collaborative practice, while B incorrectly erases profession-specific scope and education.
candidate.source_claim_supported: IPEC competencies are designed to prepare health-professions learners for interprofessional collaboration and teamwork in person/client-centered care and population health.
